Transactions must be evaluated within milliseconds to prevent unauthorized activities while minimizing false positives that frustrate legitimate users."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"System Architecture Overview"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A robust real-time fraud detection pipeline generally consists of three main phases: data ingestion, feature engineering, and model inference. Apache Kafka is commonly used for ingestion, Redis or Apache Cassandra for low-latency feature stores, and a lightweight ML model (like XGBoost or a neural network) deployed via a REST or gRPC service for inference."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Feature Engineering for Fraud Detection"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Raw transaction data alone is rarely sufficient. We need to derive behavioral features on the fly, such as transaction velocity (e.g., number of transactions in the last 10 minutes) and location deviations."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd

def calculate_velocity(user_history_df, current_timestamp, window_minutes=10):
    cutoff_time = current_timestamp - pd.Timedelta(minutes=window_minutes)
    recent_txs = user_history_df[user_history_df['timestamp'] >= cutoff_time]
    return len(recent_txs)"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Model Training with Imbalanced Data"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Fraudulent transactions typically represent less than 1% of total transaction volume. Training a model on heavily imbalanced data requires specialized techniques such as SMOTE, cost-sensitive learning, or evaluating models using PR-AUC (Precision-Recall Area Under Curve) instead of standard accuracy."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"from xgboost import XGBClassifier

model = XGBClassifier(
    n_estimators=100,
    max_depth=5,
    scale_pos_weight=100,  # Handles class imbalance
    eval_metric="aucpr"
)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Low-Latency Deployment"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep feature extraction close to the memory cache to maintain latency under 50 milliseconds."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use ONNX or TensorRT runtimes for faster model inference when dealing with deep learning architectures."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Implement circuit breakers in your microservice architecture to gracefully fallback to rule-based systems if the ML model times out."}]
